citations.description: test_persist_and_log_counts_failures_in_live_without_a_manifest drives the real _persist_and_log and checks result dict, but does not call run_pass or assert exit code
The exit code gate (if failures > 0: return 1) that the test must reach but does not
Existing fail-loud exit test stubs reconcile_once — the pattern the criterion says must not be the only coverage

findings.criterion: A test drives the REAL `reconcile.py` LIVE tally path end-to-end to the exit code — not a stubbed `reconcile_once` return. RED before the fix.
findings.detail: `test_live_mode_failure_tally.py` contains two tests that drive the real functions: `test_live_emit_returns_tally_and_still_removes_the_manifest` calls the real `apply_planning._emit_mode_manifest` and verifies the tally dict, and `test_persist_and_log_counts_failures_in_live_without_a_manifest` calls the real `reconcile._persist_and_log` and verifies `result["mutation_failures"] == 2` and `result["mutations_applied"] == 1`. Neither test goes further to call `run_pass` and assert the exit code. The criterion explicitly requires "end-to-end to the exit code" — the test stops at the result dict returned by `_persist_and_log`, not at the `if failures > 0: return 1` branch in `__main__.run_pass` (line 446). All other fail-loud exit-code tests (`test_fail_loud_exit_and_preflight.py`, `test_main_truthful_tally.py`) stub `reconcile_once` to return `mutation_failures` directly, which is exactly the pattern the criterion says must NOT be the only coverage.
findings.remediation: Add a test in `test_live_mode_failure_tally.py` (or a new file) that: (1) stubs `applier.apply` to return a tally dict `{"applied_count": 1, "failed_count": 2}` (simulating LIVE's `_emit_mode_manifest` return), (2) stubs the other reconcile_once dependencies (fetcher, differ, binding_store, health, etc.) minimally, (3) calls the real `reconcile.reconcile_once` so the real `_persist_and_log` runs and produces `mutation_failures == 2`, (4) passes that result through the real `run_pass` and asserts `rc == 1`. This exercises the full chain from the LIVE tally seam to the exit code without stubbing `reconcile_once`.
